method: The wheel is read from the note rather than from the text that was typed: a note letter A to G with up to two sharps or flats gives a pitch class from 0 to 11, and the mode picks one of two twelve-entry tables that map each pitch class to a wheel position. The minor table puts 1 at A flat, 2 at E flat, 3 at B flat, 4 at F, 5 at C, 6 at G, 7 at D, 8 at A, 9 at E, 10 at B, 11 at F sharp and 12 at C sharp. The major table puts 1 at B, 2 at F sharp, 3 at D flat, 4 at A flat, 5 at E flat, 6 at B flat, 7 at F, 8 at C, 9 at G, 10 at D, 11 at A and 12 at E. Both tables are the circle of fifths: each step from one number to the next is seven semitones, so 8A is A minor and 9A is E minor, and the major key at a number is the relative major of the minor key there, three semitones above its tonic, which is why 8B is C major. A position is written as its number plus A for a minor key or B for a major key, so A minor is 8A and C major is 8B. Open Key labels the same wheel seven positions earlier, so its number is the Camelot number minus seven, wrapped into 1 to 12: 8A becomes 1m, 1A becomes 6m and 12A becomes 5m, with m for minor and d for major. The name shown is the spelling the wheel uses, so a typed G sharp minor is reported as A flat minor on 1A with the typed spelling called out, C flat major is shown as B major and B sharp major as C major, all of which share a pitch class. The listing gives four keys: the same position, the next position (one number on, a perfect fifth up), the previous position (one number back, a fifth down, wrapping from 1 to 12) and the same number with the other letter, which is the relative major or relative minor and shares all seven notes of the scale. Input is one of three forms: a note with an optional mode (A minor, F#m, Bb major, or a bare note that means major), a Camelot code from 1A to 12B, or an Open Key code from 1m to 12d. After the note a lowercase m means minor and the words min, minor, maj and major are accepted; a lone capital M is refused rather than guessed at, because it means major in some charts and is read as minor in others. Mixed sharps and flats, a mode word that is not a mode, a number outside 1 to 12 and text that is neither a note nor a code are refused with the problem named. The page runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access, and the reference table of all 24 positions is built from the same tables as the result so the two cannot disagree.

sources.title: Mixed In Key, Interactive Camelot Wheel: the 24 keys run 1A to 12B, A is minor and B is major, 8A is A minor and 8B is C major, the relative key keeps the number and switches the letter, and one number up or down is the adjacent key.
beaTunes, Open Key Notation: a key harmonizes with itself and with X plus or minus one, d means Dur (major) and m means Moll (minor), and the number can be kept while switching d for m.

ImmerGround, The Camelot wheel explained: the full 1 to 12 table with each minor and major key and its Open Key code, each step clockwise a perfect fifth, and the Open Key number found by adding five to the Camelot number and subtracting twelve when it passes twelve.
